question: Does holding scheduled swing progression during truthful stance-support loss prevent unsupported scheduling without preventing recontact or worsening walking?
controlled_change: Preview the unchanged shared scheduler's next limb clocks and gate counters. On active waves, if any current or proposed phase is 0..72 and any proposed-stance phase 73..359 lacks explicit present-and-bearing contact, hold all four gait clocks and gate counters at their incoming values. Preserve the parent's explicit evidence-limit mode transition. Continue the ordinary steering update, V42 reference/latch math and bounded joint commands at the held phases. No measured body or contact substitution, controller gain, cap, or force estimate.
hold_lifecycle: A fresh clear state proceeds immediately. A held state requires three consecutive clear observations before resuming; an interrupted clear dwell resets to zero. Count each held command, including the first two clear-dwell commands. Permit at most 120 held commands; another required hold returns safe no actuation, an explicit support_progression_hold_timeout and unchanged input memory. A ready third clear sample may release at the limit. Inactive waves or absence of any current/proposed swing disable/reset this interlock. Runtime semantic-step and sample-time progression still apply while gait clocks are held.
parameter_provenance: Three clear samples and 120 held commands reuse the existing scheduler's MINIMUM_GATE_DWELL_STEPS and MAXIMUM_GATE_HOLD_STEPS as prospective engineering limits. They are not tuned from V42's outcomes, contact thresholds, guarantees of stability or changes to any acceptance criterion.
memory_receipts: Distinct V43 policy/profile/memory/actuation identities. Optional support_progression memory is required only by V43: held_steps and clear_dwell_steps, initially zero, with checked domains. Older policies omit it and refuse crossed data. Every successful V43 command retains incoming/proposed/selected phases, original contact observations, required stance limbs, missing support, hold choice, limits and incoming/next counters. Missing, malformed, contradictory or crossed inputs refuse without modifying input memory.
verification: Core tests cover phase 0/72/73/wrap, missing/present-nonbearing support, hold, interrupted three-sample release, zero amplitude, 120-command limit, malformed memory, original gate behavior and finite nonzero motor commands during holds.

Actual native exported interfaces consume every original V42 input for one-command checks. A separately reported chained-memory check must stop at the first refusal, if any, preserving it rather than splicing or resetting the sequence. No saved input check predicts a new trajectory.

Byte-compare older policies against the immutable V42 runtime and preserve all six recovery fixtures. Validate stateful/stateless agreement and independently reconstruct decision, phases and bounded command math.

Component profile is non-runnable. Shared worker/reader integration and the complete applicable safety gate precede any separately selected fresh physical attempt. Do not clone the harness, extend V42, change its evaluator or promote a development result.
risks: A phase hold may fail to restore support, prolong a missing contact, reduce forward progress, alter steering or cause a bounded refusal. The inherited upright reference can remain geometrically inappropriate for a missing foot. An initial swing already in progress is held, not undone. Force-aware whole-body recovery and successful three-engine kick recovery remain unproved.
